newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ eases after takeover rumours fade.
newsitem.headline: ANZ eases after takeover rumours fade.

text.p: Shares in Australian and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd fell 22.2 cents to A$9.56 on Friday, following a 56.2 cent run on Thursday on rumours of a potential takeover.

Dealers said there was little news to drive the trade, but noted rival big four bank Westpac Banking Corp, which has also been the subject of takeover rumours, was up 29.7 cents at A$7.66 at 3.25 p.m. (0525 GMT).
"Let's say it's their turn," said a Brisbane-based broker.
Traders have said a number of overseas banks could be interested in either ANZ or Westpac, variously citing ABN Amro, Ing Bank, National Westminster Plc or HSBC Holdings.

The rumour mill has included reports that a foreign bank has applied to the Australian government for permission to bid for one of the banks, which would cost in the vicinity of A$15 billion. Each has assets of mor than A$100 billion but analysts said any bid would include at least A$6 billion of goodwill.

Westpac may also have been boosted by on-going doubts over whether it would receive permission from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to take over the Bank of Melbourne Ltd, one trader said.
ANZ soared as high as A$10.00 on Thursday before profit-taking and an announcement from the bank saying it was unaware of any reason for the rise in its share price cut the rise.
Westpac shares rose sharply last Thursday on similar rumours of a takeover, and concerns about the Bank of Melbourne ruling.
